entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:163819
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 48159 of 2021

Applicant :- Chhotelal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Brij Lal Shukla

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Brij Lal Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned
Brief Holder for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 41 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B, 316 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Manikpur, District Chitrakoot during pendency of the trial.
3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased in July, 2019 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for demand of motorcycle and golden chain and on 31.03.2021 they have committed her murder for want of dowry.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and entire allegation of demand of dowry and torture made against him is totally false and baseless and actually deceased committed suicide only due to the reason that some altercation took place Chhotelal vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66743553/
1 between her and her mother-in-law i.e. mother of the applicant.
He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
He further submits that applicant is in jail since 03.04.2021 i.e. for more than two years and trial of the case could not be concluded.

5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and applicant failed to provide any plausible explanation with regard to the death of his wife, therefore, he does not deserve bail.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Although, applicant is in jail since 03.04.2021 i.e. for more than two years but he is husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.

Further, in the entire bail application, applicant failed to provide any plausible explanation that why his wife committed suicide and applicant in paragraph-15 of the affidavit very casually stated that as some altercation took place between deceased and her mother-in-law, therefore, she committed suicide.
The defence taken by the applicant appears to be vague and general in nature and merely on such defence entire prosecution story cannot be disbelieved at this stage.

8. Further, applicant is facing trial under Section 304B IPC and minimum punishment under Section 304B IPC is seven years, which may be extended up to the life imprisonment and applicant is in jail only for last two years.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant, who is husband, is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected.

11. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 11.8.2023 AK Pandey  Chhotelal vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66743553/
